label.en: Escort Leader of the Inner Attendant Directorate

units.zh: 宦者四
units.en: Eunuchs 4
units.literal: Eunuchs 4

units.zh: ○邵成章藍珪
units.en: ○ Shao Chengzhang and Lan Gui
units.literal: ○ Shao Chengzhang, Lan Gui

units.zh: 〈（康履附）〉
units.en: (with Kang Lu appended)
units.literal: (Kang Lu appended)

units.zh: 馮益張去為陳源甘王德謙關禮董宋臣
units.en: Feng Yi, Zhang Quwei, Chen Yuan, Gan Bian, Wang Deqian, Guan Li, and Dong Songchen
units.literal: Feng Yi, Zhang Quwei, Chen Yuan, Gan Bian, Wang Deqian, Guan Li, Dong Songchen

units.zh: 邵成章，欽宗朝內侍也。
units.en: Shao Chengzhang was a palace eunuch of the Qinzong reign.
units.literal: Shao Chengzhang was an inner attendant of the Qinzong reign.

units.zh: 帝入青城，命成章衛皇太子赴宣德門稱制行事。
units.en: When the emperor entered Qingcheng, he ordered Chengzhang to guard the crown prince at Xuande Gate and proclaim regency.
units.literal: When the emperor entered Qingcheng, he ordered Chengzhang to escort the crown prince to Xuande Gate to proclaim regency and conduct affairs.

units.zh: 太子北去，成章留于汴。
units.en: The crown prince went north, and Chengzhang stayed behind at Bian.
units.literal: The crown prince went north; Chengzhang remained at Bian.

units.zh: 康王將即位，元祐太后遣成章奉乘輿、服御至南京，從幸揚州。
units.en: When Prince Kang was about to take the throne, Empress Dowager Yuanyou sent Chengzhang with the imperial carriage and regalia to Nanjing, then followed the court to Yangzhou.
units.literal: When Prince Kang was about to ascend, Empress Dowager Yuanyou sent Chengzhang to present the imperial carriage and regalia at Nanjing, then followed the court to Yangzhou.

units.zh: 金人掠陝西、京東諸郡，群盜起山東，黃潛善、汪伯彥匿不以聞。
units.en: Jurchen forces overran Shaanxi and the eastern capital region; bandit armies sprang up across Shandong; yet Huang Qianshan and Wang Boyan suppressed the reports and never told the emperor.
units.literal: The Jurchens raided the prefectures of Shaanxi and Jingdong; bandits rose in Shandong; Huang Qianshan and Wang Boyan concealed the reports and did not inform [the court].

units.zh: 及張遇焚真州，去行在六十里，帝亦不之知也。
units.en: When Zhang Yu torched Zhenzhou—only sixty li from the traveling court—the emperor still knew nothing of it.
units.literal: When Zhang Yu burned Zhenzhou, sixty li from the mobile court, the Emperor likewise did not know of it.

units.zh: 成章上疏條具潛善、伯彥之罪曰，必誤國，且申潛善等使聞之。
units.en: Chengzhang memorialized with a detailed bill of charges against Qianshan and Boyan, declaring they would ruin the dynasty, and even made sure the accused heard what he had written.
units.literal: Chengzhang submitted a memorial itemizing the crimes of Qianshan and Boyan, saying they would surely bring disaster on the state, and moreover had Qianshan and the others informed so they would hear of it.

units.zh: 帝怒，除名，南雄州編管。
units.en: The emperor flew into a rage, erased his name from office, and exiled him to registered supervision in Nanxiong Prefecture.
units.literal: The Emperor was enraged, struck his name from the rolls, and banished him to supervised residence in Nanxiong Prefecture.

units.zh: 侍御史馬伸言：“成章緣上書得罪，今是何時，以言為諱？”
units.en: Remonstrance Bureau attendant Ma Shen said, “Chengzhang is being punished for memorializing the throne—what moment in our history is this, that honest speech has become forbidden?”
units.literal: Remonstrance Bureau attendant Ma Shen said: “Chengzhang offended by submitting a memorial; what time is this, to treat speech as taboo?”

units.zh: 久之，帝思成章忠直，召赴行在，其徒忌之，譖於帝曰：“邵九百來，陛下無歡樂矣！”
units.en: In time the emperor remembered Chengzhang’s loyalty and summoned him back to court; his enemies slandered him to the throne: “Shao the Nine Hundred is on his way—Your Majesty will never enjoy yourself again!”
units.literal: After a long while the Emperor recalled Chengzhang’s loyalty and forthrightness and summoned him to the mobile court; his faction resented him and slandered him to the Emperor, saying: “Shao the Nine Hundred is coming—Your Majesty will have no more pleasures!”

units.zh: 遂止之於洪州。
units.en: So they kept him stranded at Hongzhou.
units.literal: They thereupon detained him at Hongzhou.

units.zh: 金人入洪，聞其名，訪求得之，謂之曰：“知公忠正，能事吾主，可坐享富貴。”
units.en: When the Jurchens took Hongzhou they heard his reputation, hunted him down, and said, “We know you for a loyal man—serve our sovereign and you may live out your days in riches.”
units.literal: When the Jurchens entered Hong, hearing his name they sought him out by inquiry and said to him: “Knowing you are loyal and upright, if you can serve our lord you may sit and enjoy wealth and honor.”

units.zh: 成章不應，脅之以威，亦不從。
units.en: Chengzhang would not answer; they menaced him with violence, and still he refused.
units.literal: Chengzhang did not respond; they threatened him with force, yet he still would not follow.

units.zh: 金人曰：“忠臣也，吾不忍殺。”
units.en: The Jurchens said, “He is a true loyalist—we cannot bring ourselves to kill him.”
units.literal: The Jurchens said: “A loyal minister—we cannot bear to kill him.”

units.zh: 遺之金帛而去。
units.en: They left him gold and silks and went their way.
units.literal: They left him gold and silks and departed.

units.zh: 藍珪、康履，初皆為康王府都監、入內東頭供奉官，嚐從康王使金人行營。
units.en: Lan Gui and Kang Lu had both begun as chief stewards of Prince Kang’s household and as Inner Entering Eastern Head attendants-in-waiting; they had accompanied the prince on embassy to the Jurchen camp.
units.literal: Lan Gui and Kang Lu at first were both chief stewards of the Prince of Kang’s establishment and Inner Entering Eastern Head Attendant-in-Waiting; they had once followed the Prince of Kang on embassy to the Jurchen encampment.

units.zh: 及開元帥府，並主管機宜文字。
units.en: When the marshal’s headquarters was established, both were put in charge of confidential military paperwork.
units.literal: When the Marshal’s headquarters was opened, both supervised military dispatches.

units.zh: 朝廷遣人趣師入援，履等請王留相州，王叱之而行。
units.en: The court urged the prince’s army to hurry north in relief; Lu and his fellows begged him to stay at Xiangzhou; the prince scolded them and moved on.
units.literal: The court sent men urging the army to march in relief; Lu and the others asked the Prince to remain at Xiangzhou; the Prince rebuked them and marched.

units.zh: 既 即位，二人俱恃恩用事，履尤妄作威福，大將如劉光世等多曲意事之。
units.en: After his accession both men traded on old favor to run affairs; Lu in particular lorded it over everyone, and commanders such as Liu Guangshi routinely humored them.
units.literal: Once he had ascended the throne, the two men both relied on favor to handle affairs; Lu especially threw his weight about arrogantly, and great generals such as Liu Guangshi often bent to please them.

units.zh: 帝知之，詔內侍不許與統兵官相見，違者停官編隸。
units.en: The emperor learned of this and ordered that palace eunuchs must not meet army commanders on pain of dismissal and banishment.
units.literal: The Emperor knew of it and decreed that inner attendants were not permitted to meet commanders of armies; violators would be stripped of office and registered for exile.

units.zh: 履終無所忌憚，與內侍曾擇淩忽諸將，或 踞坐洗足，立諸將於左右，聲喏甚至馬前，故疾之者眾。
units.en: Lu remained utterly fearless; with the eunuch Zeng Ze he insulted field commanders—sometimes sprawling barefoot while washing, making generals stand at his side and bark their salutes even at his horse’s head—so hatred of him spread wide.
units.literal: Lu to the end had no scruples, and with the inner attendant Zeng Ze belittled the generals; sometimes he sat with legs sprawled washing his feet, had the generals stand at his sides, and made them shout their salutes even before his horse—hence many hated him.

units.zh: 俄遷內侍省押班、金州觀察使。
units.en: Soon he was promoted to Escort Leader in the Inner Attendant Directorate and made Military Commissioner of Jinzhou.
units.literal: Shortly he was transferred to Escort Leader of the Inner Attendant Directorate and made Military Commissioner of Jinzhou.

units.zh: 帝在揚州，金兵卒至，帝馳馬出門，百官不戒備，從行者惟履 等五六人。
units.en: At Yangzhou Jurchen troops appeared without warning; the emperor bolted through the gate while the bureaucracy was caught flat-footed—only Lu and five or six others rode with him.
units.literal: The Emperor was at Yangzhou when Jurchen troops suddenly arrived; the Emperor galloped out the gate; the hundred officials were unprepared; those who followed were only Lu and some five or six others.

units.zh: 自是履等益自衒，愈有輕外朝心。
units.en: From that day Lu and his circle preened all the more and looked on the civil bureaucracy with open contempt.
units.literal: From this Lu and the others showed themselves off all the more and grew ever more contemptuous of the outer court.

units.zh: 及幸浙，道吳江，其黨競以射鴨為樂。
units.en: When the court fled into Zhe and passed the Wu River, his followers made a contest of shooting ducks.
units.literal: When the court moved to Zhe, passing Wu River, his clique vied to shoot ducks for sport.

units.zh: 比至杭州，江下觀潮，中官供帳，赫然遮道。
units.en: Reaching Hangzhou to watch the Qiantang bore, eunuch supply pavilions lined the road in ostentatious display.
units.literal: By the time they reached Hangzhou, viewing the tidal bore on the river, the eunuchs’ supply tents blazed across the road.

units.zh: 統製苗傅等切齒曰：“此輩使天子 至此，猶敢爾邪？”
units.en: Commander Miao Fu and his men ground their teeth: “These creatures brought the Son of Heaven to this pass—how dare they still strut so?”
units.literal: Commander Miao Fu and others gnashed their teeth and said: “This lot drove the Son of Heaven to this pass—yet they still dare behave so?”

units.zh: 傅幕客王世修亦疾中官恣橫，以告武功大夫劉正彥，正彥曰：“會當共除之。”
units.en: Fu’s adviser Wang Shixiu, who also loathed eunuch insolence, told Military Merit Grandee Liu Zhengyan; Zhengyan said, “We will destroy them together when the moment comes.”
units.literal: Fu’s staff adviser Wang Shixiu likewise hated the eunuchs’ arrogance and told Military Merit Grandee Liu Zhengyan; Zhengyan said: “We shall jointly remove them when the time comes.”

units.zh: 王淵躋樞筦，正彥以為由宦者所薦，愈不平，謀遂決。
units.en: Wang Yuan was vaulted to Bureau Commissioner; Zhengyan believed eunuchs had engineered the promotion, grew angrier still, and the conspiracy was sealed.
units.literal: Wang Yuan vaulted to Bureau Commissioner; Zhengyan thought this was because eunuchs had recommended him and grew all the more resentful—the plot was settled.

units.zh: 伏兵斬 淵，遣兵圍履家，分捕中官，凡無須者皆殺之。
units.en: Hidden soldiers cut down Wang Yuan; troops encircled Lu’s house and hunted eunuchs throughout the city—every beardless man they found was killed.
units.literal: Ambush troops beheaded Yuan; they sent troops to surround Lu’s house, split up to seize eunuchs, and all who were beardless were killed.

units.zh: 履馳入白帝，傅等至，厲聲曰：“陛下信任中官，凡中官所主者皆得美官。
units.en: Lu raced in to warn the emperor; Fu and his men arrived shouting, “Your Majesty trusts eunuchs—every office a eunuch touches turns into a lucrative post.
units.literal: Lu galloped in to report to the Emperor; when Fu and the others arrived they said in harsh voices: “Your Majesty trusts eunuchs—every post a eunuch controls wins a fine office.

units.zh: 王淵遇賊不戰，交康履得樞 密。
units.en: Wang Yuan fled from the enemy without fighting, yet traded on Kang Lu and won the Bureau Commissioner’s seal.
units.literal: Wang Yuan met the bandits and did not fight; through association with Kang Lu he obtained Bureau Commissioner.

units.zh: 中官在外者已誅，更乞康履、藍珪、曾擇等誅之，以謝三軍。”
units.en: The eunuchs outside the palace are already dead—we now demand Kang Lu, Lan Gui, Zeng Ze, and the rest be killed to satisfy the armies.”
units.literal: The eunuchs outside have already been executed; we further beg that Kang Lu, Lan Gui, Zeng Ze, and the rest be executed to appease the three armies.”

units.zh: 帝不忍，除傅等官以安之。
units.en: The emperor could not bear to do it and enfeoffed Fu and his allies to calm them.
units.literal: The Emperor could not bear it and enfeoffed Fu and the others with offices to appease them.

units.zh: 傅等曰：“欲遷官，第須控兩匹馬與內侍，何必至此！”
units.en: Fu retorted, “Had you only wanted rank, holding two horses for a eunuch would have sufficed—why drive us to mutiny!”
units.literal: Fu and the others said: “If you only wanted promotions, you need only hold two horses for a eunuch—why come to this!”

units.zh: 帝問百 官：“策安出？”
units.en: The emperor turned to his ministers: “What is to be done?”
units.literal: The Emperor asked the hundred officials: “Where does the strategy lie?”

units.zh: 主管浙西機宜文字時希孟曰：“中官之為患，至此極矣。
units.en: Shi Ximeng, supervisor of Western Zhe military dispatches, said, “Eunuch misrule has reached its limit.
units.literal: Supervisor of Western Zhe Military Dispatches Shi Ximeng said: “The harm of eunuchs has reached this extreme.

units.zh: 不除之，天下之患未已。”
units.en: Unless they are uprooted, the realm will never know peace.”
units.literal: If they are not removed, the empire’s troubles will not cease.”

units.zh: 軍器監葉宗諤言：“陛下何惜一康履，不以慰三軍？”
units.en: Armory Director Ye Zongwu said, “Why spare a single Kang Lu when the armies are howling for blood?”
units.literal: Director of the Armory Ye Zongwu said: “Why does Your Majesty begrudge one Kang Lu and not comfort the three armies?”

units.zh: 帝不得 已，遣人執履至，履望帝呼曰：“大家何獨殺臣？”
units.en: With no choice left, the emperor had Lu seized; Lu stared at the throne and wailed, “Great One, why kill only me?”
units.literal: The Emperor had no choice; he sent men to seize Lu and bring him; Lu looked at the Emperor and cried: “Great One, why kill your servant alone?”

units.zh: 遂以付傅，即腰斬之。
units.en: He was handed to Fu and immediately cut in two at the waist.
units.literal: He was handed over to Fu and at once cut in two at the waist.

units.zh: 梟其首。
units.en: His head was spiked for public display.
units.literal: His head was displayed.

units.zh: 帝幸睿聖宮，傅等留內侍十五人奉左右。
units.en: The emperor withdrew to Ruishèng Palace; Fu left only fifteen eunuchs in attendance.
units.literal: The Emperor visited Ruishèng Palace; Fu and the others left fifteen inner attendants to serve at his side.

units.zh: 尋捕珪、擇等，皆編置遠州；
units.en: Soon Gui, Ze, and others were arrested and banished to remote prefectures;
units.literal: Shortly they arrested Gui, Ze, and the rest, all banished to distant prefectures;

units.zh: 擇，昭 州，行一程，追還斬之。
units.en: Ze, bound for Zhao Prefecture, was pursued after one day’s march, brought back, and beheaded.
units.literal: Ze, [sent to] Zhao Prefecture, after one stage on the road was pursued, brought back, and beheaded.

units.zh: 傅等誅，贈履官，諡榮節，召珪等還。
units.en: After Fu’s faction was destroyed, Lu was posthumously enfeoffed with the title Rongjie; Gui and the others were summoned back.
units.literal: When Fu and the others were executed, Lu was posthumously enfeoffed and given the posthumous title Rongjie; Gui and the rest were recalled.

units.zh: 中書舍人季陵言：“中官復召，其黨與相賀，氣焰益張，中外切齒。”
units.en: Palace draftsman Ji Ling warned, “Recall the eunuchs and their clique celebrates—insolence redoubles, and court and country grind their teeth in rage.”
units.literal: Palace Draftsman Ji Ling said: “With eunuchs recalled, their faction congratulates one another and their arrogance grows—within and without grind their teeth.”

units.zh: 不報。
units.en: The memorial went unanswered.
units.literal: No response.

units.zh: 珪至，自 武功大夫擢內侍省押班。
units.en: When Gui returned he vaulted from Military Merit Grandee to Escort Leader of the Inner Attendant Directorate.
units.literal: When Gui arrived he was promoted from Military Merit Grandee to Escort Leader of the Inner Attendant Directorate.

units.zh: 慈寧宮建，命提點事務，尋升內侍省都知。
units.en: He supervised construction of Cining Palace, then rose to Director of the Inner Attendant Directorate.
units.literal: When Cining Palace was built he was ordered to supervise affairs; shortly he rose to Director of the Inner Attendant Directorate.

units.zh: 及迎太后，命充都大主管。
units.en: When the empress dowager was escorted home he was made chief superintendent of the reception.
units.literal: When welcoming the Empress Dowager he was appointed chief superintendent in overall charge.

units.zh: 太后既還宮，珪奏應幹補授恩，乞聽慈寧宮施行。
units.en: After her return Gui memorialized to shower favors on the palace staff and asked that Cining Palace issue the appointments itself.
units.literal: After the Empress Dowager had returned to the palace, Gui memorialized on granting favors to the staff and begged that Cining Palace be allowed to carry them out.

units.zh: 從之。
units.en: The request was granted.
units.literal: It was granted.

units.zh: 珪初與履同 進，而驕橫不及履，故幸以壽終。
units.en: Gui had risen with Lu, but never matched his swagger; thus he was lucky to die in bed.
units.literal: Gui had advanced together with Lu at first, yet his arrogance did not match Lu’s; therefore he was fortunate to die a natural death.

units.zh: 有安石者，與同姓，為內侍省副都知，至景福殿使、湖州觀察使。
units.en: Another clansman, Anshi, became Vice Director of the Inner Attendant Directorate, then Palace Attendant of Jingfu Hall and Military Commissioner of Huzhou.
units.literal: There was one Anshi, of the same surname, who became Vice Director of the Inner Attendant Directorate, reaching Palace Attendant of Jingfu Hall and Military Commissioner of Huzhou.

units.zh: 卒，贈保寧軍節度使，諡良恪。
units.en: At his death he was posthumously made Military Commissioner of Baoning Circuit with the posthumous title Liangke.
units.literal: On his death he was posthumously made Military Commissioner of Baoning Circuit and given the posthumous title Liangke.

units.zh: 渡江後，中官贈諡自安石始。
units.en: After the court fled south, posthumous ennoblement of eunuchs began with Anshi.
units.literal: After crossing the Yangtze, posthumous titles for eunuchs began with Anshi.

units.zh: 又有與履同姓者名諝，為內侍省押班，亦親幸用事，與知閣門事藍公佐善，每邀公佐至其直舍，必縱飲大醉，薄莫乃歸，嚐漏泄禁中語。
units.en: Another Lu clansman named Xu, also Escort Leader, shared the emperor’s favor and power; he befriended Gate Affairs Commissioner Lan Gongzuo, entertained him nightly until both were drunk, and once leaked palace secrets.
units.literal: There was also one of the same surname as Lu named Xu, Escort Leader of the Inner Attendant Directorate, likewise favored and wielding power; he was friendly with Gate Affairs Commissioner Lan Gongzuo; whenever he invited Gongzuo to his duty quarters he would drink heavily until drunk, returning only at dusk; he once leaked forbidden-palace talk.

units.zh: 劉光遠被劾，諝與內侍陳永錫受其金，力為營救。
units.en: When Liu Guangyuan was impeached, Xu and eunuch Chen Yongxi took his bribes and fought to save him.
units.literal: When Liu Guangyuan was impeached, Xu and the inner attendant Chen Yongxi accepted his gold and strove to rescue him.

units.zh: 言官劾之，帝詔永錫與祠，諝送吏部。
units.en: Censors impeached them; the emperor gave Yongxi a temple stipend and sent Xu to the Ministry of Personnel.
units.literal: Remonstrance officials impeached them; the Emperor decreed Yongxi given a temple stipend and Xu sent to the Ministry of Personnel.

units.zh: 後累官至均州觀察使。
units.en: He later rose step by step to Military Commissioner of Junzhou.
units.literal: Later he rose by stages to Military Commissioner of Junzhou.

units.zh: 卒，贈保信軍節度使，諡忠定。
units.en: At death he was posthumously enfeoffed Military Commissioner of Baoxin Circuit with the title Zhongding.
units.literal: On his death he was posthumously made Military Commissioner of Baoxin Circuit and given the posthumous title Zhongding.

units.zh: 馮益，康王邸舊人也。
units.en: Feng Yi was a veteran of Prince Kang’s household.
units.literal: Feng Yi was an old man of the Prince of Kang’s establishment.

units.zh: 王即位，自入內東頭供奉官遷至幹辦禦藥院，尋兼幹辦皇城司。
units.en: When the prince became emperor he rose from Eastern Head attendant to superintendent of the Imperial Pharmacy, then also of the Imperial City Office.
units.literal: When the Prince ascended the throne he rose from Inner Entering Eastern Head Attendant-in-Waiting to Superintendent of the Imperial Pharmacy, and shortly also served as Superintendent of the Imperial City Office.

units.zh: 恃舊恩驕恣。
units.en: He traded on old intimacy and grew insolent.
units.literal: He relied on old favor and was arrogant and unrestrained.

units.zh: 帝幸浙東，益與御前右軍都統製張俊爭渡，以語侵俊，且訴於帝。
units.en: During the flight to eastern Zhe he quarreled with Right Army Commander Zhang Jun over a ferry crossing, insulted him, and appealed to the emperor.
units.literal: When the Emperor visited eastern Zhe, Yi vied with Right Army Commander-in-Chief Zhang Jun for passage on the crossing, insulted Jun in speech, and moreover complained to the Emperor.

units.zh: 事下御史台，侍御史趙鼎言：“明受之變，起於內侍，覆轍不可不戒。”
units.en: The case went to the Censorate; attendant Zhao Ding said, “The Mingshou mutiny began with eunuchs—we dare not forget that lesson.”
units.literal: The matter was sent to the Censorate; Remonstrance Bureau attendant Zhao Ding said: “The Mingshou mutiny arose from inner attendants—the lesson must not be forgotten.”

units.zh: 事乃已。
units.en: The matter was dropped.
units.literal: The affair then ceased.

units.zh: 紹興三年，授武功大夫、康州防禦使、帶禦器械。
units.en: In Shaoxing year 3 he was made Military Merit Grandee, Defender of Kangzhou, and Bearer of the Imperial Arms.
units.literal: In the third year of Shaoxing he was made Military Merit Grandee, Defender of Kangzhou, and Bearer of the Imperial Arms.

units.zh: 時帝用侍御史常同言，詔皇城司並隸台察，益言非祖宗舊制，帝為追寢前詔。
units.en: The emperor, heeding attendant Chang Tong, had placed the Imperial City Office under censorial oversight; Yi protested that this broke ancestral practice, and the emperor rescinded the order.
units.literal: At the time the Emperor followed Remonstrance Bureau attendant Chang Tong’s advice and decreed that the Imperial City Office likewise be subject to censorial investigation; Yi said this was not the ancestral institution; the Emperor revoked the prior decree for him.

units.zh: 特遷宣政使。
units.en: He was specially promoted to Palace Political Commissioner.
units.literal: He was specially promoted to Palace Political Commissioner.

units.zh: 益自言藩邸舊吏，乞 加恩，遂升明州觀察使。
units.en: Calling himself an old prince’s retainer, he begged extra favor and was made Military Commissioner of Mingzhou.
units.literal: Yi said of himself that as an old retainer of the princely establishment he begged added favor and was thereupon raised to Military Commissioner of Mingzhou.

units.zh: 內廄舊有騏驥院官，益請別置禦馬院，自領其事，又擅穿皇城便門。
units.en: He asked to split off a new Imperial Horse Office from the old Qiji Stud and run it himself, and without permission pierced a private gate through the palace wall.
units.literal: The inner stables formerly had officials of the Qiji Stud; Yi requested a separate Imperial Horse Office and personally directed it, and moreover on his own authority opened a convenience gate in the Imperial City.

units.zh: 侍御史沈與求以為言，趙鼎等皆患之。
units.en: Attendant Shen Yuyu protested; Zhao Ding and others were deeply alarmed.
units.literal: Remonstrance Bureau attendant Shen Yuyu spoke on this; Zhao Ding and others were all troubled by him.

units.zh: 會劉豫揭榜山東，言益遣人收買飛鴿，因有不遜語。
units.en: Liu Yu posted placards in Shandong claiming Yi was buying carrier pigeons and adding seditious slogans.
units.literal: It happened that Liu Yu posted placards in Shandong saying Yi sent men to buy carrier pigeons, with disrespectful words besides.

units.zh: 張浚請斬益以釋謗，帝不許。
units.en: Zhang Jun demanded Yi’s execution to silence the slander; the emperor refused.
units.literal: Zhang Jun requested beheading Yi to dispel slander; the Emperor did not permit it.

units.zh: 鼎言事關國體，當解職加罰。
units.en: Zhao Ding said the affair touched national dignity and Yi should be stripped and punished.
units.literal: Ding said the matter touched the dignity of the state and he ought to be removed from office and punished.

units.zh: 帝喜曰：“聞益交關外事，漸不可長。”
units.en: The emperor said gladly, “I hear Yi is meddling abroad—such conduct cannot be indulged.”
units.literal: The Emperor said with pleasure: “I hear Yi has dealings in foreign affairs—this cannot be allowed to grow.”

units.zh: 與祠放歸。
units.en: He was given a temple stipend and sent home.
units.literal: He was given a temple stipend and sent home.

units.zh: 浚意未息，鼎解之。
units.en: Zhang Jun was still unsatisfied; Zhao Ding calmed him.
units.literal: Jun’s intent was not yet quieted; Ding pacified him.

units.zh: 益自是家居廩祠者十四年。
units.en: Yi thereafter lived at home on temple grain for fourteen years.
units.literal: From this Yi thereafter lived at home on a grain stipend for fourteen years.

units.zh: 先是，偽柔福帝姬之來，自稱為王貴妃季女，益自言嚐在貴妃閤，帝遣之驗視，益為所詐，遂以真告。
units.en: Earlier, when the impostor Princess Roufu appeared claiming to be Consort Gui’s youngest daughter, Yi said he had served in the consort’s quarters; the emperor sent him to verify; the woman duped him and he declared her genuine.
units.literal: Earlier, when the false Princess Roufu came, calling herself the youngest daughter of Consort Gui of Wang, Yi said he had once been in the consort’s pavilion; the Emperor sent him to verify; Yi was deceived by her and thereupon reported her genuine.

units.zh: 及事覺，益坐驗視不實，送昭州編管，尋以與皇太后連姻得免。
units.en: When the fraud was exposed he was banished to Zhao Prefecture for false testimony, then pardoned through kinship with the empress dowager.
units.literal: When the affair came to light, Yi was punished for a false verification and sent to registered supervision in Zhao Prefecture; shortly, because of marriage ties with the Empress Dowager, he was pardoned.

units.zh: 十九年，卒於家。
units.en: In year 19 he died at home.
units.literal: In the nineteenth year he died at home.

units.zh: 張去為，內侍張見道養子也。
units.en: Zhang Quwei was the adopted son of eunuch Zhang Jiandao.
units.literal: Zhang Quwei was the adopted son of the inner attendant Zhang Jiandao.

units.zh: 初為韋太后宅提點官，累遷至安德軍承宣使、帶禦器械，又遷內侍省押班。
units.en: He began as superintendent of Empress Wei’s household, rose to Commissioner of Ande Army with Bearer of the Imperial Arms, then Escort Leader.
units.literal: At first he was superintendent of Empress Wei’s residence; he rose by stages to Commissioner of Ande Army with Bearer of the Imperial Arms, and was further transferred to Escort Leader of the Inner Attendant Directorate.

units.zh: 時見道為入內內侍省押班，父子並充景福殿使。
units.en: When Jiandao was Inner Entering Escort Leader, father and son both held Jingfu Hall attendancy.
units.literal: At the time Jiandao was Inner Entering Escort Leader of the Inner Attendant Directorate; father and son both served as Palace Attendants of Jingfu Hall.

units.zh: 去為浸有 寵，請以一官回授見道，帝嘉而許之。
units.en: Quwei gained favor and asked one promotion be transferred to his adoptive father; the emperor praised his filiality and agreed.
units.literal: Quwei gradually gained favor and requested one office be transferred back to Jiandao; the Emperor praised this and granted it.

units.zh: 其後見道以保康軍承宣使致仕，而去為與秦檜、王繼先俱用事，升延福宮使，累遷至入內內侍省都知，恃恩幹外朝謀議。
units.en: Jiandao retired as Commissioner of Baokang Army while Quwei, with Qin Hui and Wang Jixian, ran outer-court policy from Yanfu Palace up to Inner Entering Director.
units.literal: Thereafter Jiandao retired as Commissioner of Baokang Army, while Quwei together with Qin Hui and Wang Jixian wielded power; he rose to Palace Attendant of Yanfu Palace and by stages to Inner Entering Director of the Inner Attendant Directorate, relying on favor to meddle in outer-court deliberations.

units.zh: 金兵將至，遣使來，出慢言以相懼。
units.en: As Jurchen armies approached, envoys came speaking insults to frighten the court.
units.literal: When Jurchen troops were about to arrive they sent envoys who spoke slightingly to intimidate.

units.zh: 去為陰沮用兵，進幸蜀之計，宰相陳康伯力非之，帝悟而止。
units.en: Quwei secretly opposed war and urged flight to Shu; Chancellor Chen Kangbo fiercely objected; the emperor saw reason and halted the plan.
units.literal: Quwei secretly discouraged using troops and advanced a plan to move the court to Shu; Chancellor Chen Kangbo strongly opposed it; the Emperor understood and stopped.

units.zh: 侍御史杜莘老乞斬去為，以作士氣。
units.en: Attendant Du Xinlao demanded Quwei’s head to rally morale.
units.literal: Remonstrance Bureau attendant Du Xinlao begged to behead Quwei to stiffen morale.

units.zh: 先是，去為取禦馬院西兵二百人，髡其頂發，都人駭之，莘老復劾其罪。
units.en: He had seized two hundred western troops from the Imperial Horse Office and shaved their heads, shocking the capital; Xinlao impeached him again.
units.literal: Earlier Quwei had taken two hundred western soldiers from the Imperial Horse Office, shaved their crowns; the capital was appalled; Xinlao again impeached his crimes.

units.zh: 帝不得已，令去為致仕，莘老亦出補外。
units.en: The emperor ordered Quwei to retire and exiled Xinlao to the provinces.
units.literal: The Emperor had no choice; he ordered Quwei to retire; Xinlao was also sent out to an outer post.

units.zh: 及內禪，詔落致仕，提舉德壽宮，行移如內侍省，仍鑄印賜之。
units.en: At Gaozong’s abdication he was recalled, made superintendent of Deshou Palace with eunuch-grade paperwork, and given a freshly cast seal.
units.literal: At the inner abdication he was decreed to leave retirement, made Superintendent of Deshou Palace, his documents handled like those of the Inner Attendant Directorate, and a seal was still cast and bestowed.

units.zh: 修宮有勞，又特遷安慶軍承宣使。
units.en: For rebuilding the palace he was specially promoted Commissioner of Anqing Army.
units.literal: For labor in repairing the palace he was specially promoted to Commissioner of Anqing Army.

units.zh: 初，安恭後入宮，去為實進之。
units.en: Earlier he had presented Lady An Gong when she entered the palace.
units.literal: Earlier, when Lady An Gong entered the palace, Quwei had in fact presented her.

units.zh: 後崩，上皇又遣去為傳旨，立謝貴妃為後，故亦貴重，然至死不復涉朝廷事。
units.en: After her death the retired emperor used him to proclaim Consort Xie empress; he remained honored, yet never again meddled in state affairs before he died.
units.literal: After she died the Retired Emperor again sent Quwei to transmit the decree establishing Consort Xie as empress; therefore he was also esteemed, yet to his death he never again touched court affairs.

units.zh: 陳源，淳熙中提舉德壽宮，頗有寵。
units.en: In the Chunxi era Chen Yuan superintended Deshou Palace and enjoyed considerable favor.
units.literal: Chen Yuan, in the Chunxi era Superintendent of Deshou Palace, was quite favored.

units.zh: 俄帶浙西副總管，給事中趙汝愚言：“內侍不當幹軍政。”
units.en: Soon he also held Western Zhe deputy command; Giving-of-Petition Zhao Ruyu said, “Palace eunuchs must not touch military affairs.”
units.literal: Shortly he also held the post of Vice Commander-in-Chief of Western Zhe; Giving-of-Petition attendant Zhao Ruyu said: “Inner attendants ought not to meddle in military administration.”

units.zh: 遂罷。
units.en: He was removed.
units.literal: He was thereupon dismissed.

units.zh: 源恃恩顓恣，本宮書史徐彥通者為源掌家務，不數歲，官至 經武大夫；
units.en: Yuan grew tyrannical; palace clerk Xu Yantong ran his household and within years became Military Merit Grandee;
units.literal: Yuan relied on favor and was overbearing; Xu Yantong, a clerk of the palace, managed Yuan’s household affairs—in a few years he reached Military Merit Grandee;

units.zh: 甄士昌，源廝役也，工理發，奏補承信郎；
units.en: his barber Zhen Shichang was memorialized into office as Credentialed Gentleman;
units.literal: Zhen Shichang, Yuan’s menial, skilled at hairdressing, was memorialized for supplement as Credentialed Gentleman;

units.zh: 又補臨安府都吏李庚以官，使之窺伺府事。
units.en: and Capital Prefecture chief clerk Li Geng was enfeoffed to spy on the magistracy.
units.literal: he further supplemented Capital Prefecture chief clerk Li Geng with office and had him spy on prefectural affairs.

units.zh: 孝宗聞而惡之。
units.en: Xiaozong heard of it and loathed him.
units.literal: Xiaozong heard of it and detested him.

units.zh: 十年春，詔源應奉日久，特落階官，與京祠。
units.en: In spring of year 10 the emperor stripped his rank and gave him a capital temple stipend.
units.literal: In the spring of the tenth year he decreed that Yuan, having served long, was specially stripped of rank and given a capital temple stipend.

units.zh: 給事 中宇文價封還錄黃，改外祠。
units.en: Giving-of-Petition Yuwen Jia returned the draft and changed it to an outer stipend.
units.literal: Giving-of-Petition Yuwen Jia returned the recorded yellow slip and changed it to an outer temple stipend.

units.zh: 台官黃洽等又劾之，乃謫源建州居住，籍其貲進德壽宮。
units.en: Censors Huang Qia and others impeached him again; he was exiled to Jian Prefecture and his wealth was seized for Deshou Palace.
units.literal: Censorial officials Huang Qia and others again impeached him; Yuan was banished to live in Jian Prefecture and his property was registered and sent to Deshou Palace.

units.zh: 彥通除名、道州編管，士昌、庚皆抵罪。
units.en: Yantong was disbarred and banished to Daozhou; Shichang and Geng were punished.
units.literal: Yantong was struck from the rolls and banished to Daozhou for registered supervision; Shichang and Geng were all punished.

units.zh: 言者猶未已，移源郴州。
units.en: Critics were still unsatisfied and shifted his exile to Chen Prefecture.
units.literal: Remonstrators were still not satisfied and moved Yuan to Chen Prefecture.

units.zh: 源有園名「小隱」，其制視禁籞有加，高宗以賜王才人。
units.en: Yuan owned a garden called "Little Retreat" finer than the imperial park; Gaozong gave it to the Talented Lady Wang.
units.literal: Yuan had a garden called "Little Retreat" whose construction surpassed the imperial park; Gaozong bestowed it on the Talented Lady Wang.

units.zh: 光宗即位，復召還。
units.en: When Guangzong took the throne, Yuan was recalled.
units.literal: When Guangzong acceded, he was summoned back.

units.zh: 紹熙四年，自拱衛大夫、永州防禦使除入內內侍省押班。
units.en: In Shaoxi 4 he was promoted from Palace Guard Grandee and Yongzhou defense commissioner to Inner Attendant Directorate Escort Leader.
units.literal: In the fourth year of Shaoxi, he was promoted from Palace Guard Grandee and Yongzhou defense commissioner to Escort Leader of the Inner Attendant Directorate within the palace.

units.zh: 帝以疾不朝重華宮，源與內侍楊舜卿、林億年數有間言。
units.en: Ill, the emperor stopped attending Chonghua Palace; Yuan and inner attendants Yang Shunqing and Lin Yinian repeatedly traded slanders.
units.literal: The emperor, ill, stopped attending Chonghua Palace; Yuan and inner attendants Yang Shunqing and Lin Yinian often spoke ill of one another.

units.zh: 寧宗即位，命三人俱事光宗於泰安宮。
units.en: When Ningzong acceded, all three were ordered to attend Guangzong at Tai'an Palace.
units.literal: When Ningzong acceded, all three were ordered to serve Guangzong at Tai'an Palace.

units.zh: 御史章穎論其離間君親，乞行誅竄，以慰壽皇在天之靈。
units.en: Censor Zhang Ying charged them with estranging father and son, begging execution or exile to comfort the late emperor in heaven.
units.literal: Censor Zhang Ying argued they had driven a wedge between sovereign and parent, begging execution or exile to comfort Shouhuang in heaven.

units.zh: 詔罷源等官，源撫州、億年常州居住，舜卿任便居住。
units.en: An edict removed Yuan and the others from office: Yuan to Fuzhou, Yinian to Changzhou, Shunqing free to reside where he wished.
units.literal: An edict stripped Yuan and the others of office; Yuan was to live in Fuzhou, Yinian in Changzhou, and Shunqing wherever he chose.

units.zh: 慶元二年，以生皇子恩，源、億年許自便，舜卿與內祠。
units.en: In Qingyuan 2, on the birth of a prince, Yuan and Yinian were allowed free movement and Shunqing received an inner temple stipend.
units.literal: In the second year of Qingyuan, on the birth of an imperial son, Yuan and Yinian were permitted free movement; Shunqing received an inner temple stipend.

units.zh: 給事中汪義端駁之，乃移源婺州，億年湖州。
units.en: Giving-of-Petition Wang Yiduan objected, so Yuan was moved to Wuzhou and Yinian to Huzhou.
units.literal: Giving-of-Petition Wang Yiduan objected; Yuan was moved to Wuzhou and Yinian to Huzhou.

units.zh: 義端再駁舜卿內祠，反坐外補，其後源等卒聽自便。
units.en: Yiduan objected again to Shunqing's inner stipend and was himself punished with an outer appointment; afterward Yuan and the others were finally left free.
units.literal: Yiduan objected again to Shunqing's inner stipend and was punished with an outer post; afterward Yuan and the others were finally left at liberty.

units.zh: 億年養娼女以別業，源在貶所與妓濫，俱以淫媟聞，人疑其非宦者云。
units.en: Yinian kept a courtesan in a side estate; Yuan consorted with prostitutes in exile; both were notorious for debauchery, and people doubted they were real eunuchs.
units.literal: Yinian kept a courtesan in a secondary estate; Yuan consorted with prostitutes in exile; both were notorious for licentiousness, and people doubted they were true eunuchs.

units.zh: 甘昪，內侍省押班澤之子。
units.en: Gan Bian was son of Inner Attendant Directorate Escort Leader Ze.
units.literal: Gan Bian was the son of Escort Leader Ze of the Inner Attendant Directorate.

units.zh: 澤之死，累遷亦至押班。
units.en: After Ze’s death he too rose to Escort Leader.
units.literal: After Ze’s death he rose by stages also to Escort Leader.

units.zh: 乾道中，帝頗親昪，昪以此用事。
units.en: Under Qiandao the emperor favored Bian and relied on him in affairs.
units.literal: In the Qiandao era the Emperor was quite intimate with Bian, and Bian handled affairs on that account.

units.zh: 臨安尹胡與可為小官時，丐貸於臨安富民馬氏，不如欲，銜之。
units.en: Capital Prefect Hu Yuke, as a junior official, had borrowed from the rich Ma clan of Lin’an and nursed a grudge when they refused him.
units.literal: When Capital Prefect Hu Yuke was a minor official he begged a loan from the wealthy Ma family of Lin’an and was not satisfied; he harbored resentment.

units.zh: 至是，馬以鬻官鹽逾格係獄，與可諷有司以私鹽論，御史陳升卿決獄，平反之。
units.en: Now Ma was jailed for overselling government salt; Yuke steered prosecutors toward a private-salt charge; censor Chen Shengqing reversed the verdict.
units.literal: At this time Ma was imprisoned for selling official salt beyond the quota; Yuke hinted to the authorities to treat it as private salt; Censor Chen Shengqing decided the case and reversed it.

units.zh: 之子婦，與可女 也，乃陰為與可地，譖升卿於帝前，謂為豪民馬請事，所得至萬緡。
units.en: Gan’s daughter-in-law was Yuke’s daughter; she secretly paved the way for her father, telling the emperor Shengqing had taken ten thousand strings to plead for the rich Ma.
units.literal: His son’s wife was Yuke’s daughter; she secretly made room for Yuke, slandered Shengqing before the Emperor, saying he pleaded the wealthy Ma’s case and received as much as ten thousand strings of cash.

units.zh: 上疑，遂論罪，馬流嚴州，升卿由是罷去。
units.en: The emperor believed it; Ma was exiled to Yanzhou; Shengqing was driven out.
units.literal: The Emperor was suspicious; he thereupon punished the crime; Ma was exiled to Yan Prefecture; Shengqing was dismissed on this account.

units.zh: 時曾覿以使弼領京祠，王抃以知閤門兼 樞密都承旨，為入內押班，相與盤結，士大夫無恥者爭附之。
units.en: Zeng Di held a capital temple stipend as envoy deputy; Wang Bian was Gate Commissioner and Bureau Chief, also Inner Entering Escort Leader; they formed a clique that shameless officials rushed to join.
units.literal: At the time Zeng Di held a capital temple stipend as envoy deputy, Wang Bian was Gate Affairs Commissioner and also Bureau Commissioner-in-Chief, serving as Inner Entering Escort Leader; they intertwined factions, and shameless scholar-officials vied to attach themselves.

units.zh: 既而覿死抃逐，獨在，朱熹力言之，帝曰：“乃德壽宮所薦，謂有才耳。”
units.en: Di died and Bian was expelled; Gan alone remained; Zhu Xi protested fiercely; the emperor said, “Deshou Palace recommended him—they said he had talent.”
units.literal: Shortly Di died and Bian was expelled; Gan alone remained; Zhu Xi spoke forcefully on it; the Emperor said: “He was recommended by Deshou Palace—said to have talent, that is all.”

units.zh: 熹曰：“奸人無才，何以動 人主？”
units.en: Zhu Xi replied, “Villains need no talent—only audacity—to sway a ruler?”
units.literal: Xi said: “Without talent how could a villain move the ruler?”

units.zh: 用事二十年，招權市賄，黃由對策，亦頗及之。
units.en: For twenty years he sold offices and took bribes; Huang You’s examination essay denounced him too.
units.literal: He wielded power twenty years, traded power for bribes; Huang You in his policy essay also touched on this.

units.zh: 後帝察其奸，遂抵之罪，籍其貲，竟以廢死。
units.en: The emperor finally saw through him, confiscated his wealth, and he died disgraced.
units.literal: Later the Emperor detected his villainy, punished him for the crime, registered his property, and he ultimately died in disgrace.

units.zh: 弟昺，淳熙末，幹辦內東門司、帶禦器械。
units.en: His younger brother Bing, late in Chunxi, superintended the Inner Eastern Gate with Bearer of the Imperial Arms.
units.literal: Younger brother Bing, at the end of Chunxi, was Superintendent of the Inner Eastern Gate Office and Bearer of the Imperial Arms.

units.zh: 光宗朝，累遷至親衛大夫、保康軍承宣使、提舉佑神觀。
units.en: Under Guangzong he rose to Imperial Guard Grandee, Commissioner of Baokang Army, and superintendent of Youshen Abbey.
units.literal: In the Guangzong reign he rose by stages to Imperial Guard Grandee, Commissioner of Baokang Army, and Superintendent of Youshen Abbey.

units.zh: 慶元初，為內侍省都知。
units.en: At the opening of Qingyuan he became Director of the Inner Attendant Directorate.
units.literal: At the beginning of Qingyuan he became Director of the Inner Attendant Directorate.

units.zh: 帝過壽康宮，昺有力焉。
units.en: When the emperor passed through Shoukang Palace, Bing had been instrumental.
units.literal: When the Emperor passed through Shoukang Palace, Bing had strength in the matter.

units.zh: 遷官二秩，頗貴寵。
units.en: He was promoted two ranks and richly favored.
units.literal: He was promoted two ranks and was quite honored.

units.zh: 王德謙，初為嘉邸都監，頗親幸。
units.en: Wang Deqian began as chief steward of Prince Jia’s household and was warmly favored.
units.literal: Wang Deqian at first was chief steward of the Heir Apparent of Jia’s establishment and was quite intimate and favored.

units.zh: 孝宗大漸，光宗以疾久不朝重華宮。
units.en: As Xiaozong lay dying, Guangzong’s illness had kept him from Chonghua Palace for months.
units.literal: When Xiaozong was critically ill, Guangzong had long been ill and did not attend at Chonghua Palace.

units.zh: 黃由時為王府讚讀，奏請嘉王詣重華宮問疾，既得旨，德謙固請覆奏，王斥之，遂行。
units.en: Reader Huang You asked Prince Jia to visit the sick emperor; once the order came, Deqian insisted on reporting again; the prince scolded him and went.
units.literal: Huang You was then Reader-in-Waiting of the princely establishment and memorialized asking Prince Jia to go to Chonghua Palace to inquire after his health; once the decree was obtained, Deqian firmly begged to report again; the Prince rebuked him and went.

units.zh: 孝宗 崩，王在喪次，中外洶洶，王以告直講彭龜年。
units.en: When Xiaozong died the prince was in mourning; the realm seethed; he confided in lecturer Peng Guinian.
units.literal: When Xiaozong died the Prince was in mourning quarters; within and without were turbulent; the Prince told Lecturer Peng Guinian.

units.zh: 龜年以為建儲則人心安，須白中宮乃可。
units.en: Guinian said only proclaiming an heir would calm the realm, and the Central Palace must be told first.
units.literal: Guinian thought that establishing the heir would settle hearts and it was necessary to inform the Central Palace before it could be done.

units.zh: 即諭德謙奏之皇太后，德謙不敢，強之，既而無報。
units.en: He ordered Deqian to memorialize the empress dowager; Deqian shrank from it; pressed, he still brought no answer.
units.literal: He at once instructed Deqian to memorialize the Empress Dowager; Deqian did not dare; when pressed, afterward there was no reply.

units.zh: 王即位，德謙累遷昭慶軍承宣使、內侍省押班，賜居第。
units.en: After accession Deqian rose to Commissioner of Zhaoqing Army and Escort Leader and was given a mansion.
units.literal: When the Prince ascended the throne Deqian rose by stages to Commissioner of Zhaoqing Army and Escort Leader of the Inner Attendant Directorate and was granted a residence.

units.zh: 驕恣逾法，服食擬乘輿，出入或以導駕燈籠自奉。
units.en: He outstripped every statute—food and dress like the emperor’s, escorted by imperial procession lanterns.
units.literal: He was arrogant beyond the law; food and dress rivaled the imperial carriage; going out and in he sometimes had guiding lanterns for the imperial procession attend him.

units.zh: 為人求官，贓以巨萬計，泄其事者禍立至，故外朝多附之。
units.en: He sold offices for fortunes in cash; informers were ruined overnight—so the bureaucracy fawned on him.
units.literal: Seeking offices for others, bribes ran to tens of thousands; whoever leaked the matter met instant ruin—hence many in the outer court attached to him.

units.zh: 中書舍人吳宗旦事之尤謹，夜則易服造謁。
units.en: Palace draftsman Wu Zongdan served him slavishly, visiting by night in disguise.
units.literal: Palace Draftsman Wu Zongdan served him with extreme deference; at night he changed clothes to pay calls.

units.zh: 德謙求為節度使，先薦宗旦為刑部侍郎、直學士院，將使草麻。
units.en: Deqian sought a military commissionership and first secured Zongdan as Vice Minister of Justice and Hanlin academician to draft the edict.
units.literal: Deqian sought to be made Military Commissioner; he first recommended Zongdan as Vice Minister of Justice and Academician of the Hanlin Academy, intending to have him draft the patent.

units.zh: 宗旦先備草示之，引天寶、同光為比，德謙喜。
units.en: Zongdan drafted a text comparing him to the Tang eunuch generals of Tianbao and Tongguang; Deqian was delighted.
units.literal: Zongdan first prepared a draft and showed it to him, citing Tianbao and Tongguang as parallels; Deqian was pleased.

units.zh: 製出，參政何澹不肯署，諫議大夫劉德秀率台諫論列，宰相京鏜復以為言，命遂寢。
units.en: When the patent emerged, Councilor He Dan refused to countersign; Remonstrance Grandee Liu Dexiu and the censorate protested; Chancellor Jing Chung intervened—and the appointment died.
units.literal: When the patent came out, Participating Councilor He Dan refused to sign; Remonstrance and Policy Grandee Liu Dexiu led the censorate and remonstrators in protest; Chancellor Jing Chung again spoke on it—the order was shelved.

units.zh: 韓侂胄與德謙爭用事，德謙屢以計勝，侂胄擠之，詔與外祠，台諫又交章論駁。
units.en: Han Tuozhou fought him for power; Deqian outmaneuvered him until Tuozhou forced an outer temple stipend; censors piled on.
units.literal: Han Tuozhou and Deqian vied for power; Deqian repeatedly won by stratagem; Tuozhou squeezed him out; he was decreed an outer temple stipend; censors and remonstrators again submitted successive memorials of rebuttal.

units.zh: 侍御史姚愈言吳宗旦嚐草德謙製，遂罷其官。
units.en: Attendant Yao Yu noted Zongdan had drafted the patent; Zongdan was dismissed.
units.literal: Remonstrance Bureau attendant Yao Yu said Wu Zongdan had once drafted Deqian’s patent; he was thereupon dismissed from office.

units.zh: 愈又率同列力攻德謙，詔送廣德軍居 住。
units.en: Yu led colleagues in a furious attack; Deqian was ordered to reside in Guangde Army.
units.literal: Yu again led his colleagues to attack Deqian forcefully; he was decreed to reside in Guangde Army.

units.zh: 尋以臨安尹劾其贓濫僭擬，詔降團練使、移居撫州，他事勿問。
units.en: The capital prefect impeached his graft and royal pretensions; he was demoted to regiment commander and moved to Fuzhou; other charges were dropped.
units.literal: Shortly the Capital Prefect impeached his corruption, extravagance, and presumption; he was decreed reduced to Regiment Commander and moved to live in Fu Prefecture; other matters were not pursued.

units.zh: 中書舍人高文虎請改為安置，台諫復言其奸詭，乞自今不以赦移，雖特旨亦許執奏，帝用其言， 德謙遂坐廢斥以死。
units.en: Draftsman Gao Wenhu asked for “supervised residence”; censors demanded he never benefit from amnesty—even special edicts must be protestable; the emperor agreed; Deqian died in disgrace.
units.literal: Palace Draftsman Gao Wenhu begged that it be changed to supervised residence; censors and remonstrators again spoke of his treachery, begging that from now on he not be moved by amnesties—even special edicts should allow remonstrance to be filed; the Emperor used their words; Deqian ultimately sat in disgrace and died.

units.zh: 關禮，高宗朝宦者。
units.en: Guan Li was a eunuch of Gaozong’s reign.
units.literal: Guan Li was a eunuch of the Gaozong reign.

units.zh: 淳熙末，積官至親衛大夫、保信軍承宣使。
units.en: By late Chunxi he had risen to Imperial Guard Grandee and Commissioner of Baoxin Army.
units.literal: At the end of Chunxi he had accumulated office to Imperial Guard Grandee and Commissioner of Baoxin Army.

units.zh: 孝宗頗親信之，後命提舉重華宮。
units.en: Xiaozong trusted him deeply and later made him superintendent of Chonghua Palace.
units.literal: Xiaozong quite trusted him; later he was ordered Superintendent of Chonghua Palace.

units.zh: 孝宗崩，光宗疾， 不能執喪，樞密趙汝愚等請建儲以安人心，光宗禦批又有“念欲退閑”語，丞相留正懼，納祿去，人心愈搖。
units.en: When Xiaozong died Guangzong was too ill to mourn; Zhao Ruyu and others urged establishing an heir; Guangzong’s rescript even spoke of “wishing to retire”; Chancellor Liu Zheng quit in fear and the realm shook.
units.literal: When Xiaozong died Guangzong was ill and could not perform mourning; Bureau Commissioner Zhao Ruyu and others begged to establish the heir to settle hearts; Guangzong’s imperial rescript also had the words “mind set on retiring”; Chancellor Liu Zheng was afraid, submitted his salary and left; hearts grew more unsettled.

units.zh: 汝愚遣戚裏韓侂胄因內侍張宗尹以禪位之議奏，太皇太 後曰：“此豈可易言！”
units.en: Ruyu sent his kinsman Han Tuozhou through eunuch Zhang Zongyin to propose abdication; the Grand Empress Dowager said, “How can such a thing be spoken of lightly!”
units.literal: Ruyu sent his kinsman by marriage Han Tuozhou through the inner attendant Zhang Zongyin to memorialize on the plan of abdication; the Grand Empress Dowager said: “How can such a thing be spoken of lightly!”

units.zh: 明日，汝愚再遣侂胄附宗尹以奏，未獲命而侂胄退，與禮遇，禮知其意，問之，侂胄不以告。
units.en: Next day Ruyu sent Tuozhou again through Zongyin; before an answer came Tuozhou met Li; Li sensed the plot and asked; Tuozhou would not tell.
units.literal: The next day Ruyu again sent Tuozhou attached to Zongyin to memorialize; before obtaining approval Tuozhou withdrew and met Li; Li knew his intent and asked him; Tuozhou did not tell him.

units.zh: 禮指天自誓不言，侂胄遂白其事，禮即入宮， 泣告太后以時事可憂之狀，且曰：“留丞相已去，所恃者趙知院耳。
units.en: Li swore by Heaven he would keep silent; Tuozhou then confided; Li rushed in weeping to tell the empress dowager the realm was in peril: “Chancellor Liu is gone—we have only Director Zhao.
units.literal: Li pointed to Heaven and swore he would not speak; Tuozhou thereupon reported the affair; Li at once entered the palace, weeping told the Empress Dowager the worrying state of affairs, and said: “Chancellor Liu has already gone; what we rely on is Director Zhao alone.

units.zh: 今欲定大計而無太皇太后之命，亦將去矣。”
units.en: Now he seeks to settle the succession, but without your command he will leave too.”
units.literal: Now wishing to settle the great plan yet without the Grand Empress Dowager’s command, he too will leave.”

units.zh: 太后驚曰：“知院，同姓也，事體與他人異。”
units.en: She cried in alarm, “Director Zhao shares our surname—his case is not ordinary.”
units.literal: The Empress Dowager said in alarm: “The Director shares our surname—the matter is not like that of others.”

units.zh: 禮 曰：“知院未去，恃有太后耳。
units.en: Li said, “He stays only because you remain.
units.literal: Li said: “The Director has not yet left—he relies on having the Empress Dowager.

units.zh: 今有請不許，計無所出，亦惟有去而已。
units.en: Deny him now and he has no course but withdrawal.
units.literal: Now there is a request not granted—no plan emerges—and there is only leaving.

units.zh: 知院去，天下將若何？”
units.en: If Zhao leaves, what becomes of the empire?”
units.literal: If the Director leaves, what will become of the realm?”

units.zh: 太后悟，遂命禮傳旨侂胄以諭汝愚，約明日太后垂簾上其事。
units.en: She understood, ordered Li to tell Tuozhou to inform Ruyu, and set the morrow for a curtained audience.
units.literal: The Empress Dowager understood; she thereupon ordered Li to transmit the decree to Tuozhou to inform Ruyu, arranging that the next day the Empress Dowager would hold court behind the curtain and present the matter.

units.zh: 又明 日，嘉王入行禫祭，汝愚即簾前進呈禦批，太后遂命王即皇帝位。
units.en: Next day Prince Jia entered for mourning rites; Ruyu presented the rescript before the curtain; the empress dowager had the prince take the throne at once.
units.literal: Again the next day Prince Jia entered to perform the mourning rites; Ruyu at once before the curtain presented the imperial rescript; the Empress Dowager thereupon ordered the Prince to take the emperor’s seat immediately.

units.zh: 尋除禮入內內侍省都知，又差兼重華、慈福宮承受，充提舉皇城司，遷中侍大夫。
units.en: Li was made Inner Entering Director, receiver for Chonghua and Cifu palaces, superintendent of the Imperial City Office, and Palace Attendant Grandee.
units.literal: Shortly Li was made Inner Entering Director of the Inner Attendant Directorate, also concurrently Receiver for Chonghua and Cifu palaces, appointed Superintendent of the Imperial City Office, and transferred to Palace Attendant Grandee.

units.zh: 禮不以功自居，乞致仕，不許；
units.en: Li refused merit; he begged to retire—denied;
units.literal: Li did not take credit for merit; he begged to retire—not permitted;

units.zh: 乞免推恩，又不許。
units.en: he begged to decline favor extensions—also denied.
units.literal: he begged to be exempted from extended favors—not permitted either.

units.zh: 南渡後，內侍可稱者惟邵成章與禮雲。
units.en: After the flight south, only Shao Chengzhang and Li among eunuchs deserve praise.
units.literal: After the crossing south, among inner attendants who may be praised there are only Shao Chengzhang and Li.

units.zh: 董宋臣，理宗朝宦者。
units.en: Dong Songchen was a eunuch of Lizong’s reign.
units.literal: Dong Songchen was a eunuch of the Lizong reign.

units.zh: 淳祐中，以睿思殿祗候特轉橫行官。
units.en: In Chunyou he was specially promoted from Ruosi Hall attendant to lateral rank.
units.literal: In the Chunyou era, as Attendant of Ruosi Hall he was specially transferred to a lateral-rank office.

units.zh: 寶祐三年，兼幹辦佑聖觀。
units.en: In Baoyou year 3 he also superintended Yousheng Abbey.
units.literal: In the third year of Baoyou he concurrently served as Superintendent of Yousheng Abbey.

units.zh: 侍御史洪天錫劾之，不報，天錫坐左遷大理少卿。
units.en: Attendant Hong Tiansi impeached him; the memorial went unanswered; Tiansi was demoted to vice director of judicial review.
units.literal: Remonstrance Bureau attendant Hong Tiansi impeached him; no response; Tiansi was demoted to Vice Director of the Court of Judicial Review.

units.zh: 開慶初，大元兵駐江上，京師大震。
units.en: At the opening of Kaiqing Great Yuan armies camped on the Yangtze; the capital panicked.
units.literal: At the beginning of Kaiqing the Great Yuan troops were stationed on the river; the capital was greatly shaken.

units.zh: 宋臣讚帝遷幸寧海軍，簽判文天祥上疏乞誅宋臣，又不報。
units.en: Songchen urged the court to flee to Ninghai Army; signing clerk Wen Tianxiang begged for his execution—again ignored.
units.literal: Songchen urged the Emperor to move the court to Ninghai Army; Signing Clerk Wen Tianxiang submitted a memorial begging to execute Songchen; again no response.

units.zh: 景定四年，自保康軍承宣使除入內內侍省押班，尋兼主管太廟、往來國信所，同提點內軍器庫、翰林院、編修敕令所、都大提舉諸司，提點顯應觀，主管景獻太子府事。
units.en: In Jingding year 4 he rose from Commissioner of Baokang Army to Inner Entering Escort Leader, then simultaneously supervised the ancestral temple, credentials office, inner armory, Hanlin Academy, decree compilation, various grand superintendencies, Xianying Abbey, and the Jingxian Heir Apparent’s palace.
units.literal: In the fourth year of Jingding, from Commissioner of Baokang Army he was made Inner Entering Escort Leader of the Inner Attendant Directorate; shortly he also concurrently supervised the Imperial Ancestral Temple, the Credentials Office, jointly supervised the Inner Armory, Hanlin Academy, Commission for Editing Imperial Decrees, Grand Superintendent of Various Offices, Superintendent of Xianying Abbey, and Director of Affairs of the Jingxian Heir Apparent’s Palace.

units.zh: 會天祥以著作佐郎兼獻景府教授，義不與宋臣聯事，上書求去，天祥出知瑞州。
units.en: Wen Tianxiang, professor of the Jingxian palace, refused to serve with him, resigned, and was sent out as prefect of Ruizhou.
units.literal: It happened that Tianxiang as Editorial Assistant concurrently served as professor of the Jingxian palace; on principle he would not serve with Songchen and submitted a memorial begging to leave; Tianxiang was sent out as prefect of Ruizhou.

units.zh: 言者論宋臣不置，帝曲為諭解庇之。
units.en: Critics said Songchen should not hold office; the emperor excused and shielded him.
units.literal: Remonstrators discussed that Songchen should not be appointed; the Emperor bent to explain and shield him.

units.zh: 秘書少監湯漢上封事，亦言：“宋臣十餘年來聲焰薰灼，其力能去台諫、排大臣，至結凶渠以致大禍。
units.en: Secretary Vice Director Tang Han wrote, “For more than ten years Songchen’s flame has scorched the court—he removes censors, expels ministers, even joins villains to bring disaster.
units.literal: Secretary Vice Director Tang Han submitted a sealed memorial, also saying: “For more than ten years Songchen’s renown has blazed; his power can remove censors and remonstrators and expel great ministers—even joining vicious ringleaders to bring great calamity.

units.zh: 中外惶惑切齒，而陛下 方為之辨明，大臣方為之和解，此過計也。
units.en: Court and country gnash their teeth while Your Majesty explains away his crimes and ministers smooth them over—this is too indulgent.
units.literal: Within and without are fearful and gnash their teeth, yet Your Majesty is just now explaining it for him; great ministers are just now reconciling it for him—this is excessive caution.

units.zh: 願收還押班等除命，不勝宗社之幸。”
units.en: Withdraw his appointments—nothing would better secure the dynasty.”
units.literal: I beg that the appointments such as Escort Leader be withdrawn—nothing would better fortune the altars of state.”

units.zh: 疏入，帝亦不之省。
units.en: The memorial was ignored.
units.literal: When the memorial entered the Emperor likewise did not examine it.

units.zh: 六月，命主管御前馬院及酒庫。
units.en: In the sixth month he was put in charge of the imperial horse office and wine warehouses.
units.literal: In the sixth month he was ordered to supervise the Imperial Horse Office before the throne and the wine warehouses.

units.zh: 既卒，帝猶命特轉節度使，其 見寵愛如此。
units.en: After his death the emperor still posthumously made him Military Commissioner—such was the favor he enjoyed.
units.literal: After he died the Emperor still ordered him specially transferred to Military Commissioner—such was the favor he enjoyed.
